options.text: Viral infection causing inflammation, oedema, and mucus plugging of the terminal bronchioles
Inspiratory stridor from upper airway pathology
Hypotension as a pre-terminal circulatory sign
Reduced intake and fewer than 4 wet nappies in 24 hours
Rash, petechiae, bruising, and temperature on exposure

explanation: Viral infection causing inflammation, oedema, and mucus plugging of the terminal bronchioles is the correct process. This describes the underlying pathophysiology of bronchiolitis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Respiratory - Bronchiolitis

optionExplanations.A: Correct because bronchiolitis is caused by viral infection leading to inflammation, oedema, and mucus plugging of the terminal bronchioles.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because inspiratory stridor suggests upper airway obstruction, not bronchiolitis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because hypotension is a late circulatory sign, not the mechanism of bronchiolitis.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because reduced intake and fewer than 4 wet nappies are assessment findings of dehydration or severity, not the bronchiolar process.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because rash, petechiae, bruising, and temperature on exposure are not features of bronchiolitis pathogenesis.
